profiles.notes: 2027 guide checked 23 October 2026. APS points are not IB Diploma totals. Programme-specific and university-wide conditions must be read together. This is not complete institutional coverage.

requirements.label: School-leaver entry: 25 NUST APS points
requirements.details: Ordinary school-leaver route: at least 25 APS points across five subjects including NSSC Ordinary English at E or better. Current Namibian Grade 11 learners and Grade 12 learners may apply; final school-leaving certificates are also accepted for assessment. These are NUST APS points, not an IB total, and individual programmes can require more.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 6

requirements.label: IB subjects: official APS conversion, not a Diploma cutoff
requirements.details: For the IB route, HL grades 7,6,5,4,3,2,1 map to APS 10,9,8,7,6,5,4; SL grades 7,6,5,4,3,2 map to APS 8,7,6,5,4,3. APS uses five subjects including English. No minimum IB Diploma total or TOK/EE points rule is stated; do not turn APS 25/30 into IB 25/30 or infer subject equivalencies.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 5

requirements.label: GCE A/AS/O-level subject-to-APS mapping
requirements.details: For GCE qualifications, A-level A,B,C,D,E map to APS 10,9,8,7,6; AS a,b,c,d,e to APS 9,8,7,6,5; O-level A*,A,B,C,D,E,F,G to APS 8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1. The table separately puts N/O/subsidiary A-level wording in the APS-5 row; confirm that legacy category with admissions. This is grade conversion, not a universal three-A-level offer.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 5

requirements.label: NSC Mathematical Literacy is not Mathematics
requirements.details: For programmes requiring Mathematics, NSC Mathematical Literacy does not satisfy that subject requirement. No IB/AP Mathematics substitute is established by this statement.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 5

requirements.label: One complete application with a valid email
requirements.details: Submit one complete application, with required supporting documents and a valid email for admissions correspondence. Incomplete applications and faxed applications/documents are not accepted; an online form without required PDF uploads remains incomplete.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 6-7

requirements.label: Online and manual route wording needs reconciliation
requirements.details: The guide explicitly offers ordinary undergraduate online applications and describes them on page 7; mature-age, advanced-standing and resumption routes are manual only. A separate unqualified sentence on page 6 says applicants can apply only manually. Do not treat that sentence as cancellation of the explicit online route; confirm the route if unsure. Email submission is not accepted.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 6-7

requirements.label: Certified results and identity evidence
requirements.details: Provide certified school results and identity evidence: Namibian ID/birth certificate or, for non-Namibian citizens, passport. Current Grade 11/12 learners use mid-term results. Manual applicants also attach the payment receipt; subsequent final results remain necessary for final selection.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 8

requirements.label: Declaration; guardian signature if under 18
requirements.details: Accept the declaration/undertaking. On the application form a parent or legal guardian must co-sign for an applicant under 18; online acceptance is the applicant's electronic signature.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 7-8

requirements.label: 2027 application fees by submission route
requirements.details: The guide lists non-refundable undergraduate online N$150 and manual N$240 application fees, with N$690 for late applications. These are application charges, not annual tuition; the guide does not establish whether the late charge replaces or adds to the ordinary charge.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 5

requirements.label: 2027 entry: ordinary and late dates
requirements.details: Ordinary applications closed 25 September 2026; the guide lists 30 October 2026 for late applications. The ordinary date is already past at this review. The late date is not permission for mature-age late entry or proof that every programme still has space.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 5

requirements.label: Mid-year results yield provisional decisions
requirements.details: Applicants using current or upgraded mid-year results receive provisional decisions; final offers follow final results in January 2027. The guide expects November/December 2026 communications for earlier final-results, mature-age, advanced-standing and resumption applicants. Attendance on campus for final selection is needed only when invited.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 8

requirements.label: Computer Science and Informatics: Mathematics route
requirements.details: For Bachelor of Computer Science (07BCCS) and Bachelor of Informatics (07BAIN), page 12 specifies NSSCO Mathematics D or NSSCAS Mathematics E/e. The ordinary/AS grade case is preserved from the table, not converted to an IB grade. Shared condition stored once for both programmes.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 12

requirements.label: Computing faculty mature-age exception
requirements.details: The computing/informatics faculty excludes mature-age entry except for Bachelor of Journalism and Media Technology. This is route-specific, not a ban on all older applicants or an extra ordinary-entry examination.

source.title: NUST 2027 prospective students guide, printed/PDF page 11-12

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: Online application is free
requirements.details: The online undergraduate application process is free. This does not waive tuition or the enrolment commitment deposit after an offer.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: 2027/28 entry: Early Bird and Regular deadlines
requirements.details: For entry beginning August 2027, the page lists 1 December 2026 for Early Bird and 31 March 2027 for Regular. Early Bird requires the application and supporting documents by the deadline; late applications require both qualification and space. These dates are not guaranteed programme openings.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: At least 17 by December in the admission year
requirements.details: An applicant must meet matriculation requirements and be at least 17 by December of the year of admission.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: Certified copies; originals only on request
requirements.details: Submit certified academic results/records and applicable identity/name-change evidence. Authorized certifiers are a minister of religion, justice of the peace, attorney-at-law or medical practitioner. Originals are submitted only when requested; tampered evidence forfeits admission consideration.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: Identity checklist differs for overseas applicants
requirements.details: The web checklist names Jamaican birth/citizenship evidence and TRN, while the international booklet printed page 3 instead lists birth certificate and optional passport copies. Do not impose Jamaican citizenship or TRN on every overseas applicant; confirm the applicable identity documents.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: Tertiary transcripts by the document deadline
requirements.details: Where required, transcripts from previous tertiary study must arrive by the application deadline. The general page says a secondary-school transcript is unnecessary; this does not waive academic examination results or a programme-specific transcript request.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: After offer: enrolment commitment deposit
requirements.details: Acceptance is confirmed only after a non-refundable Enrolment Commitment Deposit is paid; it is credited toward university fees on enrolment. No amount is specified here.

source.title: UTech Jamaica: prospective undergraduate applicants, 2027/28

requirements.label: CSEC/GCE pass grades used in programme tables
requirements.details: The table header accepts CSEC General Proficiency grades 1-3 (grade 3 from June 1998 onward), GCE O-level A-C or equivalent qualifications, with technical qualifications assessed individually. Required subject counts and higher grades depend on the specific programme; no universal IB/AP equivalent is stated.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 15-22

requirements.label: Six computing degrees share English/Mathematics entry
requirements.details: Animation Development and Production, Applied Artificial Intelligence, Computer Information Systems, Computing, Computer Network and Security, and Gaming each list five CSEC/GCE O-level passes including English Language and Mathematics or equivalent. Stored once for this named group; Animation portfolio and Computing interview conditions remain programme-specific.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 15-16

requirements.label: Nursing and direct-entry Midwifery: shared school route
requirements.details: For BSc Nursing and BSc Midwifery (Direct Entry): five CSEC/GCE O-level passes including English, Mathematics, Biology or Human and Social Biology and two other approved subjects; no more than two subjects at grade C/3. This shared rule is stored once, not extended to post-registration nursing.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 10

requirements.label: Nursing/Midwifery: pre-entry test and interview
requirements.details: Acceptance for BSc Nursing and direct-entry BSc Midwifery requires a successful pre-entrance test and interview. No numerical test pass mark or universal competition requirement is given.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 10

profiles.notes: 2027/2028 other-route conditions, individually labelled: PLA alternative entry versus post-admission English placement/progression. They are not cumulative academic requirements for every applicant. No unverified mature-age age cutoff, IELTS score or IB waiver is added.

requirements.label: Prior Learning Assessment: relevant attainments and support
requirements.details: Applicants lacking ordinary entry may seek PLA based on relevant prior learning, attainments and/or work experience, with written support from people with first-hand knowledge of their potential. The university assesses equivalence; no universal age 25 or fixed employment duration is specified here.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 4

requirements.label: PLA may require interview and Foundation modules
requirements.details: PLA assessment may require an interview and successful Foundation modules through the UTech Jamaica Academy. These are conditional route requirements, not an interview mandate for all applicants.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 4

requirements.label: After admission: English proficiency test or exemption
requirements.details: Admitted students sit the English Language Proficiency Test unless exempt; a failed test requires passing non-credit Developmental English before university Academic Literacies. This is a post-admission placement/progression condition, not a published IELTS entrance cutoff.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 4

requirements.label: Listed exemptions from the internal English test
requirements.details: Exemption alternatives: CSEC English A grade 1; GCE O-level English A; CAPE Communication Studies grade 1/2; passed Developmental English COM0001 or a UTech Communication/Academic Writing module; recognized undergraduate degree, diploma or associate degree; or passed first-year communication modules at an associated community college/franchise. No IB-English or IELTS exemption is inferred.

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 4

source.title: UTech Jamaica international booklet: 2027/28 entry, printed page 4

requirements.label: Credit transfer: institution-sent official transcript
requirements.details: After acceptance, request the former tertiary institution to send an official transcript directly to Admissions and submit transfer-of-credit forms to the relevant faculty/college for evaluation. Credit is not automatically awarded.
